package_info.why_malicious: Multiple versions of the ua-parser-js package were compromised in a supply chain attack. Malicious code was injected into the package's postinstall lifecycle script, causing the package to download and execute cryptomining and password-stealing malware on both Linux and Windows systems. Because ua-parser-js is a widely used dependency, the attack enabled automatic infection of developer and production environments upon installation, resulting in widespread system compromise and credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (postinstall), the code uses child_process to execute a shell command that downloads a shell script from a remote server via curl and pipes it to sh, resulting in the immediate execution of the downloaded script and installation of a cryptominer or password-stealing Trojan.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes a shell command that fetches and runs a remote script during package installation, which is a well-known technique for delivering malware and is highly unusual for legitimate npm packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not execute arbitrary remote code during installation. Postinstall scripts are typically used for setup or build tasks, not for downloading and running unverified external scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download pre-built binaries for platform compatibility, but these downloads are from trusted sources, use HTTPS, and verify file integrity with checksums or signatures.
key_indicators: Use of child_process.exec to run shell commands
curl command fetching code from an untrusted remote domain
Piping downloaded script directly to sh for execution
No user interaction or consent required
No integrity or authenticity verification of downloaded code

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (postinstall), the code uses child_process to execute a PowerShell command that downloads a Windows executable from a remote server to the system temp directory and immediately runs it, resulting in the installation and execution of a password-stealing Trojan.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads a Windows binary from an untrusted remote server and executes it without user knowledge or consent, which is a classic malware delivery method and not expected in npm package installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not download and execute arbitrary binaries from untrusted sources during installation, especially without verifying the integrity or authenticity of the files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some build tools may download platform-specific helpers, but these are typically signed, downloaded over HTTPS, and verified before execution.
key_indicators: Use of PowerShell to download and execute binaries
Writes executable to system temp directory (C:\Windows\Temp\malware.exe)
No integrity or authenticity verification of downloaded binary
No user interaction or consent required

attack_chain.action: User or CI system installs the compromised ua-parser-js package, triggering the malicious postinstall script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code execution on the host system during the package installation process.

attack_chain.action: The malicious postinstall script downloads and executes a cryptominer or password-stealing Trojan, depending on the operating system.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, resource hijacking for cryptomining, and theft of credentials or other sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts invoking child_process to execute shell or PowerShell commands
Execution of shell commands that download and run remote scripts or binaries during package installation
Immediate execution of files downloaded from untrusted or unexpected domains
Lack of integrity or authenticity checks on downloaded files
file_indicators: Presence of unexpected or modified postinstall.js in node_modules/ua-parser-js
Downloaded files in system temp directories (e.g., /tmp/malware.sh, C:\Windows\Temp\malware.exe)
Unusual modifications to npm lifecycle scripts within node_modules/ua-parser-js
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to domains not associated with the legitimate ua-parser-js project (e.g., http://malicious-domain.com)
Connections to known malware distribution domains during npm install or build processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for unexpected execution of postinstall scripts, especially those invoking child_process to run shell or PowerShell commands. Flag any network activity from build or CI environments to untrusted or unexpected domains during package installation. Inspect node_modules/ua-parser-js for unauthorized or unexpected modifications to lifecycle scripts such as postinstall.js. Use endpoint protection to detect execution of downloaded binaries or scripts from system temp directories. Correlate file creation and process execution events during npm install to identify suspicious behaviors.
